title: Robust Event Collector and Evolutionary Schema Guard for Console Usage Pipeline
creator: Priya Shah
description: Context: Console emits a high-volume stream of usage events (route hits, model calls, cost metadata) into the analytics pipeline. We've seen three problems in the last quarter: (1) bursts of malformed events causing downstream job failures, (2) schema drift from client-side SDK changes, and (3) high-tail latency when validation runs synchronously in the ingest path. Goal: build a resilient event collector and an "evolutionary" schema guard that enforces hygiene without blocking healthy traffic or inflating latency and cost. The work spans backend services (collector), schema registry/validation, rollout strategy, and observability.
acceptance_criteria: Collector accepts and buffers 20k events/s with <5% p99 end-to-end added latency under typical load
Schema guard detects and classifies schema violations into: harmless-extension, warning-delta, and blocking-error
By default the pipeline operates in fail-open mode with sampling of offending events to a quarantine topic; critical blocking-error paths can be toggled to fail-closed per route
A lightweight schema registry exists (versioned JSON Schema) with an HTTP management API and audit logs
Every schema change goes through review and automated backward-compatibility checks; console UI shows recent breaking changes and impact estimates
Dashboards show per-route ingestion rate, validation error breakdown, quarantine size, and time-to-resolve for schema incidents
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Deploy a horizontally-scalable collector service (Go) that performs schema validation asynchronously using a local cache of schemas; validation runs on worker pool to keep request path fast
Phase 2: Build schema registry service (Node/Express) storing versioned JSON Schemas in GCS with signed change records; expose API for create/list/get and admin rollouts
Phase 3: Add graded validation semantics: extension-ok, warn, block. Default is extension-ok with sampled quarantine for unknown fields. Make blocking toggles at route-level via config in ConfigDB
Phase 4: Integrate with Kafka topics: raw-events -> collector -> validated-events / quarantine-events. Ensure at-least-once semantics and idempotency keys for downstream consumers
Phase 5: Observability: add metrics (validation.latency, validation.errors.by_type, quarantine.size), tracing tags for schema.version and validation.outcome, and an incident dashboard in Grafana
Phase 6: Rollout: start with 10% of traffic for sensitive routes (billing, auth), monitor errors, then progressive rollout to 100% with canned rollback steps
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema validator using a library matrix (ajv, gojsonschema) and fuzz inputs to exercise edge cases
Load tests in staging: synthetic producer at target 20k events/s sustained for 1 hour measuring p50/p95/p99 validation latency impact
Chaos test: simulate schema registry latency and verify collector degrades gracefully (local cache TTL) and doesn't block ingest
Compatibility test harness: run new schema diffs against representative historical event sample and produce a detailed compatibility report
E2E smoke: pipeline from console -> collector -> analytics job ensuring no downstream job failures for both extension-ok and warn cases
tradeoffs_and_decisions: We considered pushing full synchronous validation into the ingress (earliest possible) but deferred to async validation to preserve p95 latency goals for console requests
We will implement extension-ok (fail-open) by default because false-positives have high customer impact; blocking mode available per-route for security-sensitive flows
For schema storage we chose versioned JSON Schema in GCS vs a heavy Confluent Schema Registry to keep operational surface small and make it auditable for compliance teams
Validation library choice: use the Go-side gojsonschema for parity with runtime and a small Node shim for admin operations; performance wins outweighed using a single cross-language library
